record.name: Vladan Dobanovački
record.title: Principal Research Fellow
record.bio: Vladan Dobanovački completed his undergraduate and MSc studies in Chemistry at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, graduating in 2004 and 2006 respectively, before obtaining his PhD in Analytical Chemistry from the same institution in 2011 with a thesis on molecularly imprinted polymer films for aqueous-phase sensing. He joined the BioSense Institute in 2013 and was appointed Principal Research Fellow in 2021. His work within the Sensors and Microsystems Group centres on the preparation and characterisation of molecularly imprinted polymer layers on quartz crystal microbalance transducers, with a particular focus on surface functionalisation chemistry and receptor immobilisation strategies for detecting micropollutants, pharmaceuticals, and agrochemicals in water. He supervises doctoral and master's students and contributes to instrumentation courses at the Faculty of Sciences. He regularly works with QCM-D, AFM, XPS, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy equipment housed at the BioSense Institute cleanroom and surface characterisation laboratories.
open_to: equipment access (QCM-D, AFM, XPS at BioSense Institute)
consulting on MIP sensor design and surface functionalisation
record.industry_experience: Provided consulting to a Novi Sad-based water quality instrumentation startup during 2022–2023 on MIP receptor layer specifications for an in-line flow sensor prototype. Has participated in two industry-funded feasibility studies for food safety applications of QCM-MIP sensors.
record.notes: Dobanovački prefers collaborations that involve direct experimental work rather than purely computational or review-type contributions. He has full access to the BioSense Institute cleanroom and surface characterisation suite but scheduling requires advance notice of at least four weeks due to shared facility demand. He is currently supervising two doctoral students and has capacity for one additional industrial PhD candidate starting no earlier than autumn 2026.
